event.title: Asleep At the Wheel
event.description:
“scruffy but sincere traditionalists” – AllMusic

 

Asleep at the Wheel’s Ray Benson has been traversing the globe for over fifty years. He is an ambassador of Western swing music, introducing its irresistible sound to generation after generation. More than 100 musicians have passed through the Wheel, but Benson remains the front man and the keeper of the vision. in the process racking up more than thirty albums, ten Grammy awards and literally millions of miles on the road. 

“I’m the reason it’s still together, but the reason it’s popular is because we’ve had the greatest singers and players,” Benson explains. “When someone joins the band, I say, ‘Learn everything that’s ever been done, then put your own stamp on it.’ I love to hear how they interpret what we do. I’m just a singer and a songwriter, and a pretty good guitar player, but my best talent is convincing people to jump on board and play this music.”

Asleep at the Wheel represents an important cornerstone of American roots music. They maintain this even though some of its members and audiences represent a new generation. That far-reaching appeal remains a testament to Benson’s initial vision.

“It took me sixty years, but I’m doing what I’m meant to do—singing and playing and writing better than I ever have. A bandleader is just someone who gathers people around them to play the best music they can play. I just try and make the best decisions possible and kick some ass every night onstage.”

Recommended for fans of Bob Wills & the Texas Playboys, Kris Kristofferson, Lyle Lovett and Ernest Tubb.

There’s no better place to be right before Christmas than at Dakota with Andrew Walesch and his eighteen-piece big band. Ring in the holidays with the songs of Bennett, Sinatra, Bublé, Basie, and more!

Like a good many before him, singer and pianist Andrew Walesch manages to encapsulate the sophistication of a cosmopolite and the self-effacing charm of a country boy. Leading his all-star big band, showman Andrew Walesch kidnaps the Blue Eyes tradition and makes it his own in his jazz-bent Sinatra revue. Thus, Walesch is a traditionalist and an iconoclast rolled into one.

Whether composing and arranging or appearing in settings ranging from solo artist to big band, this St. Cloud, MN native is as respectful of his predecessors as he is ready to take a leap into the unknown and chart a new course. Additionally, Andrew routinely jams venues all over the Midwest and beyond with a uniquely cross-generational audience. Walesch’s fans include jazz enthusiasts of a certain age, as well as a younger crowd compelled by his down-home insouciance. Here, all are drawn in by the knowing irreverence of a tried-and-true American nightclub entertainer. 

“Although they are my idols, I don’t attempt to imitate the great pop and jazz artists of the 50s and ’60s,” says Andrew. “But I go for broke when we do our shows – vocally and musically!”

His vocal and piano chops, along with his keen sensibility to find and interpret a great lyric, have led to some great opportunities for Walesch. In 2023, Andrew accepted the position of artistic director of the MIM Music Theater in Phoenix, Arizona where he now resides.  

Recommended for fans of Tony Bennett, Frank Sinatra, Michael Bublé and Bing Crosby.

There’s no better place to be right before Christmas than at Dakota with Andrew Walesch and his eighteen-piece big band. Ring in the holidays with the songs of Bennett, Sinatra, Bublé, Basie, and more!

Like a good many before him, singer and pianist Andrew Walesch manages to encapsulate the sophistication of a cosmopolite and the self-effacing charm of a country boy. Leading his all-star big band, showman Andrew Walesch kidnaps the Blue Eyes tradition and makes it his own in his jazz-bent Sinatra revue. Thus, Walesch is a traditionalist and an iconoclast rolled into one.

Whether composing and arranging or appearing in settings ranging from solo artist to big band, this St. Cloud, MN native is as respectful of his predecessors as he is ready to take a leap into the unknown and chart a new course. Additionally, Andrew routinely jams venues all over the Midwest and beyond with a uniquely cross-generational audience. Walesch’s fans include jazz enthusiasts of a certain age, as well as a younger crowd compelled by his down-home insouciance. Here, all are drawn in by the knowing irreverence of a tried-and-true American nightclub entertainer. 

“Although they are my idols, I don’t attempt to imitate the great pop and jazz artists of the 50s and ’60s,” says Andrew. “But I go for broke when we do our shows – vocally and musically!”

His vocal and piano chops, along with his keen sensibility to find and interpret a great lyric, have led to some great opportunities for Walesch. In 2023, Andrew accepted the position of artistic director of the MIM Music Theater in Phoenix, Arizona where he now resides.  

Recommended for fans of Tony Bennett, Frank Sinatra, Michael Bublé and Bing Crosby.

event.title: The Bad Plus Farewell Tour Finale
event.description:
“finely orchestrated, catchy original tunes, and a knack for radically reconstituted pop covers.” – The New York Times 

 

The Bad Plus are the ultimate originals. A democratic unit with a clear vision and a refusal to conform to convention. For the past two decades, they have played with spirit and adventure and have made their own rules. Moreover, they do so with a bold sense of creativity and intent. Avoiding easy categorization, The Bad Plus has won critical acclaim and a legion of fans worldwide. Further, their unique sound and flair for live performance make them a must-see ensemble.

Now in their twenty-sixth year, The Bad Plus continues to push boundaries. Here, founding members Reid Anderson (bass) and Dave King (drums) embark on a new piano-less incarnation of the band. Also, Ben Monder (guitar) and Chris Speed (tenor saxophone) join the group, instigating a new wave of excitement and anticipation. These new voices are re-energizing their sound and inspiration. The Bad Plus have constantly searched to bridge genres and techniques. Additionally, they explore the infinite possibilities of exceptional musicians working in perfect sync.

The Bad Plus’s sixteenth release, 2024’s Complex Emotions strikes out in stunning new directions. Here, it often sounds radically different than anything the band has done before, while still maintaining the band’s vital and unmistakable identity. Credit that to all four members’ instinctual attraction to song form, the compelling immediacy of their collective improvisations. Also, yes, their willingness to drill down into the full gamut of emotional complexity. The band can veer into so much unexplored terrain yet still emerge sounding like The Bad Plus on Complex Emotions. Thus, this is a testament to their finely crafted identity and insistence on constantly evolving. 

This is The Bad Plus in their most creative and expressive form. This is The Bad Plus now.

Recommended for fans of Brad Mehldau, Joshua Redman, Bill Frisell and Kurt Rosenwinkel.

Dantzler and Graydon began as solo performers. Dantzler was born in Philadelphia and got his start in the music business writing songs for Pebbles and Bell Biv DeVoe. Graydon, from Washington, D.C., signed a solo deal at the age of 15. The two united and began writing songs, but then married and started a family. However, Dantzler went back to trying to make it on the local scene. He and Graydon began performing at the Black Lily club, where they caught the attention of Jill Scott.  

They spent the next two years working on the debut Kindred the Family Soul album, 2003’s Surrender to Love. It featured an impressive cast of collaborators, including Scott, string arranger Larry Gold, Bilal, King Britt, and Jazmine Sullivan. Thus, it was nominated for a Grammy in the category of Best R&B/Soul Album. 2005’s In This Life Together was inspired by Ruby Dee and Ossie Davis’ memoir of the same name. 2008’s The Arrival became their highest-charting title to that point. Here, it reached number sixty-seven on the Billboard 200 and number seven on the R&B Albums chart. 

2011’s Love Has No Recession features guests ranging from go-go pioneer Chuck Brown to relative newcomer BJ the Chicago Kid. Kindred’s sixth full-length, 2016’s Legacy of Love, climbed into the top fifteen of the Billboard R&B chart.

Recommended for fans of Ledisi, Eric Roberson, Avery*Sunshine and Stokley.

“there is not a band on earth that is better. Stunning.” – Flea, Red Hot Chili Peppers

Their trademark sound pays homage to the New Orleans brass band tradition. Also, they weave a tapestry that combines elements of jazz, funk, soul, R&B. Then, they incorporate more of the sounds from the streets they grew up on. Their sound has traveled from their legendary twenty-five-year run of Tuesday nights at the Maple Leaf to stages all over the world. Those auspicious beginnings have led to thousands of shows to music aficionados everywhere, including heads of state and royalty.

The band’s unique “soundtrack of New Orleans” has also garnered admiration from artists of all genres. They’ve shared the stage and collaborated with everyone from the Grateful Dead to the Red Hot Chili Peppers. Also, Maceo Parker, Green Day, U2, James Brown, 311, G-Love, MuteMath, Juvenile, Train, Big Freedia, Ani DiFranco, and Galactic. Further, Allen Toussaint, Neville Brothers, Quincy Jones and Trombone Shorty.

Recommended for fans of Trombone Shorty, The Dirty Dozen Brass Band, Kermit Ruffins and Preservation Hall Jazz Band.

event.title: Steely Dane
event.description:
“the band is energetic and sounds amazing” – Milwaukee Magazine

 

In 2010, co-founders David Adler and David Stoler (The Steely Daves) put together a tribute show for Steely Dan. There, they would feature the best musicians in the Madison, WI music scene. Madison is located in Dane County, WI, thus the name. 

The first Steely Dane show featured over thirty of Madison’s best rock and jazz musicians, and it sold out. Not ones to waste a herculean effort of arranging a full night’s worth of the Dan’s best stuff, the crew decided to do it again, and again… and oops, now it’s no longer a show, it’s a BAND. 

Since then, the band has trimmed down to the current fourteen-piece family. Now, that features a four-piece horn section, two female backup singers, two guitars, two keyboards, vibes, and percussion. Here, they have all the instruments necessary to recreate the amazing mixes of the Dan’s albums and live performances. Moreover, the band has won multiple awards for best tribute band and sold out theaters from Chicago to Minneapolis. Additionally, they are a perennial favorite at summer festivals as well. 

Their songbook features over fifty songs from both Steely Dan and Donald Fagen’s solo career. This allows them to play different shows night after night. Furthermore, they have even performed complete album shows for The Royal Scam, Aja, and Gaucho.

Recommended for fans of Steely Dan, Donald Fagen, Fleetwood Mac and The Eagles.

event.title: Marcus Miller
event.description:
“one of the cornerstones of modern electric bass” – Premier Guitar

 

Get ready for an unforgettable evening with Grammy-winning bass virtuoso, Marcus Miller! Celebrating over forty-three years of musical excellence, Marcus will be performing selections from his extensive catalog. Here, he features beloved hits that have graced the careers of Miles Davis, David Sanborn, Roberta Flack, and Luther Vandross. Moreover, prepare to be captivated as Marcus infuses each piece of music with his unparalleled arranging skills. He delivers fresh and exciting interpretations of his music that keep audiences on their toes.

Marcus’ resume speaks for itself. There, he has dozens of movie scores and over 500 recording credits to his name across jazz, R&B, and opera. Also, as a UNESCO Artist for Peace and changemaker, his work on social justice projects continues to be inspiring. In 2020, Marcus created, musically produced, and posted the “Lift Every Voice” get out the vote event. There, he brought together political leaders and musical legends to encourage political participation. Additionally, he contributed to UNESCO’s United Against Racism video alongside countless industry legends. Then, Prince Albert of Monaco commissioned him to create the orchestral arrangement for in Donny Hathaway’s “Someday We’ll All Be Free” video, which he also appeared in.

The year ahead continues to look just as busy for Marcus. Further, he is a member of the Board of Directors for the Herbie Hancock Institute of Jazz. Also, he joined Herbie for a virtual celebration of International Jazz Day on April 30th. In 2022, Marcus composed the score for the documentary film SIDNEY for Apple TV+. There, the film told the story of legendary actor, filmmaker and iconic civil rights activist, Sidney Poitier.

Recommended for fans of Miles Davis, Victor Wooten, Stanley Clarke and Jaco Pastorius.

event.title: Trio Mandili
event.description:
The world’s most viral folk trio.

 

How does a centuries-old village singing tradition become a 1-billion-view global digital phenomenon?

Meet Trio Mandili — arguably the world’s most viral folk trio.

What began as three friends singing together in the Georgian countryside grew into an extraordinary international success story. Their three-part harmonies are rooted in Georgia’s ancient polyphonic singing tradition. Accompanied by the traditional panduri, they have captivated audiences across cultures and languages.

The trio has grown quickly, garnering more than one billion views worldwide and nearly two million YouTube subscribers. Trio Mandili has built a global following extending far beyond Georgia and the Caucasus and now performs around the world.

In 2027, the trio brings its unforgettable live performance to the United States for the first time.

Whether you’ve followed their videos for years or are discovering them for the first time, this is a rare opportunity to experience the voices behind more than a billion views — live.

Recommended for fans of DakhaBrakha, Basiani Ensemble, Bani and Chveneburebi.

event.title: Talk: The Tortoise, the Hare, and the Art Market
event.description:
Free for Members, $5 for general public.

Robin Starr (Bonhams Skinner, General Manager)

Museums work at a steady, methodical pace. Exhibitions are planned months if not years in advance, patrons are cultivated over years and decades to become donors, and art is collected slowly in accordance with institutional vision. On the other hand, auction houses move like lightning, with ever-changing focuses. Entire auctions are put together and sold within two to three months. Client relationships, though often long-lasting, are usually built quickly and circumstantially and subject to the whims of the art market. Despite their difference in pace, however, museums and auction houses hold an important relationship, supplementing and supporting art, artists, and each other.

In this expert talk, Robin Starr of Bonhams Boston (formerly Skinner) will share stories about her work with museums, including a look behind the scenes at some of your favorites in the Worcester Art Museum’s collection.

event.title: Talk: The Korean Tiger, from Mountain Lords to “KPop Demon Hunters”
event.description:
Free for Members, $5 for general public

Speaker: Sunglim Kim (Associate Professor of Art History, Dartmouth University)

For centuries, the tiger has occupied a special place in Korean art and culture. Revered as the “Lord of the Mountain,” it was feared as a powerful wild animal and honored as a guardian capable of warding off evil. Tigers also appear alongside mountain spirits in religious paintings and in Korean folk painting, or minhwa, as playful, awkward, and sometimes comical creatures.

This talk explores the changing image of the Korean tiger, from sacred guardian and mountain lord to national symbol, popular mascot, and contemporary character. Over time, the tiger became closely connected to Korean cultural identity and came to be seen as an animal representing Korea and its people. The talk concludes with Derpy, the beloved blue tiger from Netflix’s KPop Demon Hunters, whose design reimagines Korean tiger-and-magpie paintings for a global audience. Through these examples, the talk considers why the tiger has remained one of the most familiar and enduring symbols of Korean culture.

About the speaker

Sunglim Kim is an Associate Professor of Art History at Dartmouth University. Her scholarship focuses on pre-modern and early 20th-century Korean art and culture. Her research interests include the rise of consumer culture in late Chosŏn dynasty and the role of the professional nouveau riche, the so-called chungin (middle people) in the production, distribution, collection, and consumption of art in 18th and 19th century Korea; artistic exchanges among China, Korea, and Japan; the shaping of images of Korea and her people during the Japanese colonial period; and the use of visual space as political tool in modern and contemporary Korea.

event.title: Know Your Worth 2nd Annual Gala
event.description:
Join the Know Your Worth Foundation for the 2026 Know Your Worth Gala on Thursday, October 1, at The LEX. This inspiring evening is dedicated to leveling the playing field for local youth through student-athlete support, mentorship and community investment. Guests will enjoy an elegant night featuring inspiring student-athlete stories, live entertainment, fine dining and a silent auction.

Proceeds from the gala directly support athletic coaching, mental health resources, nutrition and health checkups for local students, helping empower the next generation of leaders on and off the field. The evening will include a VIP reception, cocktail hour, dinner, program, keynote speaker, live performance, fund-a-need opportunity, live auction and networking.

event.title: 2026 NCPA Annual Convention
event.description:
The NCPA Annual Convention is the can’t-miss event for independent pharmacists and their teams for learning how to expand services, find efficiencies, and increase revenue. It’s more than a conference — it’s where you go to get real, practical ideas from peers who understand your business and walk away with strategies you can actually use.

From high-impact, peer-to-peer education to unmatched networking, there’s nothing else on the calendar quite like it. And the NCPA Expo Hall? One of the most diverse in the industry — packed with solutions, services, and innovations designed to help your pharmacy run more efficiently and profitably.

NCPA is accredited by the Accreditation Council for Pharmacy Education as a provider of continuing pharmacy education. This program will provide up to 12 contact hours (1.2 CEUs) of continuing pharmacy education. Sessions are knowledge and application-based and accredited for 1.0 contact hours (0.1 CEU). Participants must attend, enter an attendance code on NCPA’s learning center, and complete a feedback questionnaire in order to receive credit for the program. Target audience: community pharmacists and community pharmacy technicians.

Experience the premier event for community pharmacy
owners and their teams. #NCPA2026

event.title: Boozy Book Fest 2026
event.description:
Kansas City’s most anticipated literary event returns this fall as Boozy Book Fest brings together thousands of readers, acclaimed authors, and immersive experiences for one unforgettable day.

With 7,000+ attendees, national headliners, and a vibrant vendor marketplace, Boozy Book Fest delivers a fresh, high-energy take on the traditional book convention—designed for readers who truly love the stories.

Event Overview

Set inside Bartle Hall at the Kansas City Convention Center, Boozy Book Fest offers a dynamic, walkable experience featuring author panels, live conversations, curated vendors, and dedicated spaces for meet-and-greets and signings. From casual readers to literary enthusiasts, attendees can explore, connect, and celebrate books in an engaging, social atmosphere.

What to Expect

  • Expansive Vendor Hall: Browse a wide selection of books, merchandise, and literary-inspired goods
  • Author Panels & Conversations: Multiple stages featuring engaging discussions, panels, and fireside chats
  • Book Signings: Meet your favorite authors and get books signed in dedicated areas
  • Curated Experience: Thoughtfully designed layout with clear wayfinding for easy navigation
  • Beverage Options: Enjoy cocktails and refreshments throughout the event

Plan Your Experience

A full event map, programming schedule, and day-of details will be released in advance, allowing attendees to plan their experience and make the most of the day.

A New Chapter for Kansas City Events

Boozy Book Fest is more than a convention—it’s a celebration of storytelling, community, and culture. Whether you’re there for the panels, the signings, or the atmosphere, this is one literary event you won’t want to miss.

event.title: ACNM 2026 Annual Meeting & Exhibition
event.description:
The American College of Nurse-Midwives 71st Annual Meeting & Exhibition brings midwifery professionals from across the country to Kansas City for four days of continuing education, clinical learning, professional development, networking, and industry collaboration. The 2026 meeting will be held October 9–12 at the Kansas City Convention Center.

Centered on the theme “This Is Our Moment: Midwives Transforming the World,” the annual meeting will explore developments in midwifery practice, reproductive health, research, education, advocacy, and patient care. Programming will include expert-led workshops, plenary presentations, concurrent educational sessions, roundtable discussions, poster presentations, professional recognition ceremonies, and social events.

  • Continuing education and clinical sessions led by experienced professionals
  • Full- and half-day workshops offering hands-on, in-depth learning
  • An exhibit hall and Midwifery Market featuring industry resources and solutions
  • Research posters, lectures, awards, and professional recognition
  • Networking opportunities with midwives, educators, researchers, students, policymakers, community leaders, and allied health professionals

About ACNM

The American College of Nurse-Midwives is the professional association representing certified nurse-midwives and certified midwives in the United States. ACNM advances excellence in midwifery education and practice while supporting professionals who provide care throughout pregnancy, childbirth, postpartum recovery, newborn care, gynecologic health, family planning, and other primary and reproductive healthcare services.

The ACNM Annual Meeting & Exhibition offers a valuable opportunity for the midwifery community to exchange knowledge, build professional relationships, and advance high-quality, accessible healthcare for individuals and families nationwide.

event.title: The Original Lowrider Midwest SuperShow
event.description:
The Original Lowrider Midwest SuperShow rolls into Bartle Hall at the Kansas City Convention Center on Sunday, October 11, 2026, from 11 a.m. to 6 p.m. This consumer show celebrates lowrider culture, custom vehicles, automotive artistry and the community that keeps the scene moving.

Guests can experience a showcase of standout rides, detailed builds, creative craftsmanship and the signature style that makes lowrider culture so iconic. Whether you are a longtime enthusiast, a car club member, a custom-car fan or attending for the first time, The Original Lowrider Midwest SuperShow offers an exciting day of cars, culture and community in downtown Kansas City.

event.title: Baddies & Bosses Concert
event.description:
Baddies & Bosses Live in Concert brings a major night of hip-hop energy to Municipal Auditorium on Saturday, October 17, 2026. Presented by STASHHOUSE KD, this one-night-only concert features a stacked lineup with BossMan Dlow, Plies, Kash Doll, Skilla Baby, KenTheMan and Kalii all performing live on one stage.

Fans can expect a high-energy evening packed with big performances, crowd favorites and nonstop entertainment in the heart of downtown Kansas City. Grab your crew, get your fit together and be in the building for one of the city’s can’t-miss concert events of the year.

event.title: Jack Henry Connect 2026
event.description:
Jack Henry Connect 2026 comes to Kansas City for a milestone conference celebrating innovation, inspiration, and connection within the financial services technology community. Hosted at the Kansas City Convention Center, this annual educational conference and technology showcase brings together Jack Henry clients, partners, industry professionals, and solution providers for three days of learning, networking, and collaboration.

The 2026 event marks a special celebration of 50 years of Jack Henry, highlighting the company’s ongoing commitment to connecting people with financial institutions and financial institutions with solutions that help serve their communities. Attendees can expect powerful keynote presentations, hands-on learning opportunities, networking experiences, and technology-focused programming designed to inspire meaningful progress across the industry.

What to Expect

  • Educational sessions and hands-on learning opportunities
  • Keynote presentations and industry insights
  • Networking with peers, partners, and financial technology professionals
  • A technology showcase featuring solutions for financial institutions
  • Special programming celebrating Jack Henry’s 50th anniversary

Event Details

Event: Jack Henry Connect 2026
Dates: October 19–21, 2026
Location: Kansas City Convention Center
City: Kansas City, Missouri

Connecting Innovation and Community

Jack Henry Connect is more than a conference—it is a gathering designed to strengthen relationships, share ideas, and explore solutions that support the future of financial services. event.title: Phantom of the Opera
event.description: Cameron Mackintosh and LW Entertainment are delighted to reveal the first video look into the North American Tour of the new production of Andrew Lloyd Webber’s legendary musical, PHANTOM OF THE OPERA. The North American Tour company stars in the first video look with Isaiah Bailey in the title role of ‘The Phantom of the Opera,’ Jordan Lee Gilbert as ‘Christine Daaé,’ and Daniel Lopez as ‘Raoul,’ Midori Marsh as ‘Carlotta Giudicelli,’ William Thomas Evans as ‘Monsieur Firmin,’ Carrington Vilmont as ‘Monsieur André,’ Lisa Vroman as ‘Madame Giry’ Christopher Bozeka as ‘Ubaldo Piangi,’ Melo Ludwig as ‘Meg Giry.’ Alexa Xioufaridou Moster plays the role of ‘Christine Daaé, at certain performances.’ In addition, the entire second year schedule of tour cities has been announced and includes Tempe, Las Vegas, Dallas, Nashville, Pittsburgh, Cleveland, Philadelphia and Boston. The full schedule is listed below. Additional first year tour cities and information can be found at ThePhantomOfTheOpera.com, the official global website for PHANTOM OF THE OPERA.. Cameron Mackintosh said, “I’m really delighted to bring Andrew Lloyd Webber’s PHANTOM OF THE OPERA back to thrill American audiences once again after its phenomenal record-breaking run on Broadway. When I unveiled this new production in London after the pandemic many of our brilliant original creative team, including Hal Prince, Gillian Lynne and Maria Björnson, were sadly no longer with us. Our exciting new team, inspired by their predecessors’ glorious work, updated certain aspects of the production that resulted in a dazzlingly fresh version of the much-loved original, which was rapturously received by audiences and critics alike. So, as we raise our even more sensational chandelier across North America, you can once again thrill to Andrew’s soaring music of the night and be swept away by a revitalized PHANTOM in all its glory!”

event.title: Book Talk with Sonny Buttar, author of Daughters of Rosebud
event.description:
Left Bank Books and the Left Bank Books Foundation are delighted to present St. Louisan Sonny Buttar’s debut novel, The Daughters of Rosebud (2026).
Join us at High Low Literary Arts Cafe to welcome Sonny Buttar for a presentation and book signing, free and open to the public. Sonny will be in conversation with St. Louis author and Board Chair of Kimbilio for Black Fiction, David Haynes.

The Daughters of Rosebud is a powerful exploration of sisterhood, family loyalty, and the courage it takes to heal. Teacher Salma Chaudhry lives a quiet life, avoiding all attachments. Growing up in small-town Rosebud, Salma and her older sister Asma were inseparable, but amid their mother’s decline and their parents’ rigid expectations, Asma makes a choice that tears the family apart. The fallout changes everything–and forces Salma to choose between her sister and her parents. Salma has spent years trying to forget. But as she recollects her past and considers reconciliation with her father, a young student opens a surprising connection to Asma’s past. In finally facing her history, Salma finds the bravery to love and hope again.

event.title: Soul Siren Playhouse Presents: “The Niceties” by Eleanor Burgess
event.description:
Set within the walls of a prestigious Northeastern university, what starts as a routine conference between Zoe, a Black scholar, and her tenured history professor, Janine, unravels into all-out intellectual warfare over Zoe’s thesis that the American Revolution would not have been successful without slavery in America. What starts as critiques on grammatical structure spirals into judgments on historical accuracy, erasure, professional ethics, and who ultimately is allowed to set the standard for Truth.

What happens when legitimate critique and systemic bias present themselves simultaneously? How do we reconcile when the pursuit of being right becomes so entangled with race, history, institutions, and public ideology that we stop being capable of seeing one another outside the argument? It’s all in “The Niceties.”

event.title: Soul Siren Playhouse Presents: “The Niceties” by Eleanor Burgess
event.description:
Set within the walls of a prestigious Northeastern university, what starts as a routine conference between Zoe, a Black scholar, and her tenured history professor, Janine, unravels into all-out intellectual warfare over Zoe’s thesis that the American Revolution would not have been successful without slavery in America. Memory, illusion, and longing blur as each character reaches for a better life. The Glass Menagerie is a luminous, deeply moving classic of the American stage.

event.description: An eclectic group of six mid-pubescents vie for the spelling championship of a lifetime. While candidly disclosing hilarious and touching stories from their home lives, the tweens spell their way through a series of (potentially made-up) words, hoping never to hear the soul-crushing, pout-inducing, life un-affirming “ding” of the bell that signals a spelling mistake. Six spellers enter; one speller leaves a champion!
